At Moneybox, our mission is to give everyone the means to get more out of life. We’re guided by our belief that wealth isn’t about the money, it’s about the means to more – more freedom, opportunities, possibilities, and peace of mind.

Moneybox is an award-winning wealth management platform, helping over one and a half million people build wealth throughout their lives, whether they’re saving and investing, buying their first home, or planning for retirement.

Job Brief

At Moneybox, we help over a million people save and invest for their future. Behind the scenes, our 450+ colleagues rely on our in-house Workplace Tech team to give them the tools they need to do their best work.

We’re a small, hands-on team that takes ownership and gets things done. From setting up a new joiner’s first laptop to managing the security and identity tools that protect an FCA-regulated business, we make sure our technology works for everyone.

We’re looking for a proactive Workplace Tech Analyst to join us. You’ll be a go-to person for colleagues when technical issues arise, taking ownership and making sure problems are resolved properly. You’ll see the impact of your work every day, with opportunities to develop your skills in security, identity and infrastructure as the team evolves.

Hybrid working & hours

This role is based in our London office for three days and two days from home per week.
Hours are: 09:00 to 17:30 with 08:00 to 16:30 being required once a month (first Thursday of the month)

What you'll do

As a Workplace Tech Analyst, you'll be at the heart of our Workplace Tech team, ensuring our 450+ employees have the tools and tech support they need to succeed. We're an FCA-regulated business, so security and access control matter: getting the details right is as important as getting things fixed quickly. Here’s a snapshot of how you’ll contribute:
  • Be the first point of contact for all tech-related queries, turning employee challenges into effective solutions.
  • Own your tickets from pickup to closure, keeping requesters and the team updated with clear notes at every stage and keeping our Service Level Agreements (SLAs) front and centre.
  • Flag blockers early and ask for help when you're unsure. We’d rather hear about a problem on day one than discover it on day five.
  • Work closely with the wider team to escalate and resolve more complex issues, ensuring a smooth handover.
  • Actively listen to understand issues thoroughly and translate them into clear, actionable technical resolutions.
  • Handle access requests with care, applying least-privilege and role-based access principles across our systems.
  • Contribute to and maintain our internal knowledge base by documenting solutions, creating 'how-to' guides, and sharing best practices to empower staff with self-service options.
  • Help our new starters hit the ground running by running our weekly group onboarding sessions (in person and remote) and delivering smooth tech setups, and ensure a thorough, auditable offboarding process for leavers.
  • Keep our meeting rooms and video conferencing kit in top shape with regular checks and proactive monitoring.
  • Maintain a well-organised and secure inventory of our laptops and other tech equipment in our asset management system.
  • Lend a hand with project work, including security and infrastructure projects, providing support whenever extra resources are needed.

Who you are

  • A driven, ambitious individual who’s looking to build their career at an exciting, very fast-growing company.
  • Has a genuine interest in technology and using it to help people work effectively.
  • Reliable and responsive: you follow through on what you say you’ll do and keep people in the loop.
  • Comfortable working autonomously, with the judgement to know when to check in or escalate.
  • Security-minded: you understand why access controls, audit trails and compliance training matter in a regulated business, and treat them as part of the job.
  • Naturally personable, great communicator who has a passion for their work and the people they work with.
  • Knows how to have fun whilst maintaining a professional outlook.

Experience and skills

  • Experience with ticketing systems (ideally Freshservice) and keeping support tickets updated with clear, useful notes.
  • Experience with Google Workspace, plus familiarity with SSO and password management tools such as 1Password.
  • Comfortable supporting both Mac and Windows environments, ideally with exposure to MDM tools such as Iru (formally Kandji) and Microsoft Intune / Entra ID.
  • Basic knowledge of iOS and Android devices.
  • An understanding of least-privilege and role-based access control (RBAC).
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Ability to describe technical fixes in an easy-to-understand way.
  • Clear, friendly written and verbal communication, and confidence presenting to small groups.
  • Nice to have: experience with CrowdStrike, Cloudflare Zero Trust, Snipe-IT, Slack administration, or scripting and automation (e.g. GAM, Bash, PowerShell).

What's in it for you

  • Opportunity to join a fast-growing, award-winning and super ambitious company

  • Work with a friendly team of highly motivated individuals

  • Be in an environment where you are listened to and can actually have an impact

  • Thriving, collaborative, and inclusive company culture

  • Mission + Functional team socials every 8 weeks

  • Company pension scheme

  • Company bonus scheme

  • Health Cash Plan (cashback on visits to the dentist & opticians etc.)

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Wellhub subscription to a variety of gyms and wellbeing apps

  • Enhanced parental pay & leave

  • 25 days holiday + bank holidays with additional days added with length of service.

  • This is a hybrid role. Our office is in London, by the Oxo Tower

Our Commitment to DE&I:
At Moneybox, we promote, support and celebrate inclusion, diversity and equity for all, so that everyone can bring their full selves to work. We believe that diversity drives innovation, and that if our team is representative of our community of customers, we can better support their needs. description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist based in India.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist to manage provider enrollment, credentialing, and medical billing operations in a remote healthcare environment. In this role, you will coordinate with insurance payers, healthcare providers, and internal teams to ensure accurate documentation, timely claims processing, and reliable reimbursement. You will oversee credentialing applications and renewals while maintaining compliance with payer requirements and applicable healthcare regulations. Your expertise in insurance billing, coding, and claims resolution will help minimize denials and prevent delays in provider network participation. You will also monitor payment discrepancies, maintain comprehensive records, and identify opportunities to improve revenue cycle processes. This is an opportunity to contribute to efficient healthcare administration while supporting providers and delivering operational accuracy.

Accountabilities:

As a Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist, you will oversee the full lifecycle of provider credentialing, insurance enrollment, and claims management. You will ensure that provider records remain accurate, billing activities meet payer requirements, and reimbursement issues are addressed promptly through effective coordination and follow-up.

  • Prepare and submit credentialing applications for new healthcare providers across commercial insurance carriers, Medicare, Medicaid, and managed care organizations.

  • Manage provider re-credentialing within required timelines to prevent lapses in insurance network participation.

  • Maintain accurate provider information in credentialing databases, payer portals, and related systems.

  • Coordinate with providers to collect required documentation, professional licenses, certifications, and signatures.

  • Review, prepare, and submit medical insurance claims accurately using electronic health record (EHR) and billing systems.

  • Apply appropriate CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes, including relevant modifiers, in accordance with applicable billing guidelines.

  • Verify patient demographics, insurance eligibility, and coverage details before submitting claims.

  • Apply payer-specific policies, fee schedules, and filing deadlines to support accurate and timely claims processing.

  • Monitor claim status through payer portals, manage claim edits and rejections, and coordinate necessary adjustments.

  • Post insurance payments, contractual adjustments, and write-offs accurately, identifying underpayments and payment discrepancies.

  • Reconcile daily, weekly, and monthly payment reports and maintain accurate billing records.

  • Investigate claim denials and rejections, prepare supporting documentation, and submit timely appeals.

  • Maintain detailed follow-up logs to track outstanding claims through resolution.

  • Ensure compliance with HIPAA, CMS requirements, payer policies, and applicable federal and state regulations.

  • Collaborate with clinical, administrative, and revenue cycle teams to resolve billing and credentialing issues.

  • Serve as a liaison between healthcare providers and insurance payers, resolving enrollment discrepancies and network participation issues.

  • Monitor changes in payer requirements, credentialing policies, and coding guidelines to maintain compliance.

  • Maintain credentialing logs, spreadsheets, databases, and expiration-date trackers to ensure deadlines are met.

  • Audit credentialing files for completeness and accuracy and prepare management reports on application progress, pending items, and compliance status.

  • Identify recurring payer issues and recommend process improvements to strengthen operational efficiency and reimbursement outcomes.

title: Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist based in Germany.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist to manage provider enrollment, credentialing, and medical billing operations in a remote healthcare environment. In this role, you will coordinate with insurance payers, healthcare providers, and internal teams to ensure accurate documentation, timely claims processing, and reliable reimbursement. You will oversee credentialing applications and renewals while maintaining compliance with payer requirements and applicable healthcare regulations. Your expertise in insurance billing, coding, and claims resolution will help minimize denials and prevent delays in provider network participation. You will also monitor payment discrepancies, maintain comprehensive records, and identify opportunities to improve revenue cycle processes. This is an opportunity to contribute to efficient healthcare administration while supporting providers and delivering operational accuracy.

Accountabilities:

As a Medical Insurance Credentialing Specialist, you will oversee the full lifecycle of provider credentialing, insurance enrollment, and claims management. You will ensure that provider records remain accurate, billing activities meet payer requirements, and reimbursement issues are addressed promptly through effective coordination and follow-up.

  • Prepare and submit credentialing applications for new healthcare providers across commercial insurance carriers, Medicare, Medicaid, and managed care organizations.

  • Manage provider re-credentialing within required timelines to prevent lapses in insurance network participation.

  • Maintain accurate provider information in credentialing databases, payer portals, and related systems.

  • Coordinate with providers to collect required documentation, professional licenses, certifications, and signatures.

  • Review, prepare, and submit medical insurance claims accurately using electronic health record (EHR) and billing systems.

  • Apply appropriate CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes, including relevant modifiers, in accordance with applicable billing guidelines.

  • Verify patient demographics, insurance eligibility, and coverage details before submitting claims.

  • Apply payer-specific policies, fee schedules, and filing deadlines to support accurate and timely claims processing.

  • Monitor claim status through payer portals, manage claim edits and rejections, and coordinate necessary adjustments.

  • Post insurance payments, contractual adjustments, and write-offs accurately, identifying underpayments and payment discrepancies.

  • Reconcile daily, weekly, and monthly payment reports and maintain accurate billing records.

  • Investigate claim denials and rejections, prepare supporting documentation, and submit timely appeals.

  • Maintain detailed follow-up logs to track outstanding claims through resolution.

  • Ensure compliance with HIPAA, CMS requirements, payer policies, and applicable federal and state regulations.

  • Collaborate with clinical, administrative, and revenue cycle teams to resolve billing and credentialing issues.

  • Serve as a liaison between healthcare providers and insurance payers, resolving enrollment discrepancies and network participation issues.

  • Monitor changes in payer requirements, credentialing policies, and coding guidelines to maintain compliance.

  • Maintain credentialing logs, spreadsheets, databases, and expiration-date trackers to ensure deadlines are met.

  • Audit credentialing files for completeness and accuracy and prepare management reports on application progress, pending items, and compliance status.

  • Identify recurring payer issues and recommend process improvements to strengthen operational efficiency and reimbursement outcomes.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate combines hands-on medical credentialing and billing experience with a strong understanding of insurance payer processes, coding standards, and healthcare compliance. You should be highly organized, comfortable managing multiple deadlines, and able to communicate effectively with providers, insurance representatives, and internal stakeholders.

    • High school diploma or equivalent required; an associate or bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, or a related field is preferred.

    • At least two years of experience in medical credentialing, medical billing, or both, preferably working with multiple insurance payers.

    • Strong working knowledge of commercial insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, and managed care credentialing and reimbursement processes.

    • Familiarity with CAQH ProView, NPPES, PECOS, Availity, payer portals, and EHR or medical billing software.

    • Demonstrated experience preparing accurate claims, resolving denials, following up on outstanding payments, and maintaining compliance with payer requirements.

    • Understanding of CPT, ICD-10, and HCPCS coding systems, including modifier requirements.

    • Knowledge of provider enrollment, re-credentialing procedures, insurance eligibility verification, claim submission deadlines, and payer-specific policies.

    • Medical billing or coding certification, such as Certified Professional Biller (CPB), Certified Professional Coder (CPC), or an equivalent qualification, is an advantage.

    • Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining accurate, complete, and well-organized records.

    • Strong organizational, time-management, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple applications, claims, and deadlines simultaneously.

    • Effective written and verbal communication skills for coordinating with healthcare providers, insurance representatives, patients, and colleagues.

    • Proficiency in credentialing, billing, and documentation systems, with the ability to learn new tools and workflows.

    • Understanding of HIPAA, CMS, NCQA, and other applicable healthcare compliance standards.

    • Ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining productivity, accuracy, and consistent follow-through.

      • Benefits:

      • Fully remote work arrangement.

      • Full-time employment.

      • Opportunity to develop expertise across provider credentialing, medical billing, insurance claims, and revenue cycle operations.

      • Collaborative work with healthcare providers and administrative, clinical, and revenue cycle professionals.

title: Strategic Communications Lead, EMEA
description:
FM, a leading mutual insurance company established nearly two centuries ago, is dedicated to property risk management and resilience for its policyholder-owners—many of the world’s largest organizations, including one in four Fortune 500 companies. Our mission combines scientific research, engineering expertise, and insurance protection to help clients prevent property loss and maintain business continuity through cost-effective risk management strategies.

We are seeking an experienced, results-oriented communications professional to serve as the Strategic Communications Lead for the EMEA region. This role will lead external communications, media relations, thought leadership, executive visibility and storytelling efforts across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. They will be key in supporting FM’s global public relations and marketing objectives with a focus on earned media. Working closely with regional business leaders, subject matter experts, marketing colleagues, and agency partners, this individual will develop and execute coordinated communications programs that generate meaningful external visibility for FM through earned media, industry speaking opportunities, executive thought leadership, and strategic content.

The ideal candidate is an experienced communications professional with a background in agency and/or large corporate environments. They are intellectually curious, highly proactive, and relentlessly focused on results. They possess exceptional news judgment, strong business acumen, and a proven ability to identify opportunities that elevate both organizations and their leaders.

Collaborating with marketing colleagues, business leaders, SMEs, and agency partners to develop and implement PR and thought leadership in support of business and marketing strategies. Key responsibilities include:

External Communications Strategy

  • Understanding business issues, objectives, and priorities and align communications activities to the needs of targeted audiences, delivering the right message to the right audience at the right time.
  • Lead planning for PR and thought leadership activities that support FM’s reputation, business growth and marketing objectives in EMEA.
  • Effectively balance timely delivery of materials for individual PR activities, programs and campaigns, providing agile support for unexpected priorities, and maximizing resources across the year.

Media Relations

  • Providing oversight and guidance for EMEA-based PR agencies, media opportunities, and external communications activities to protect and enhance FM’s reputation.
  • Develop and execute proactive media relations programs that elevate FM's visibility and reinforce the company's authority in the industry.
  • Build relationships with key media contacts, Tier 1 journalists, and identify opportunities for interviews, commentary, feature stories, and other earned media placements.

Thought Leadership and Executive Visibility

  • Work with FM’s executives and subject matter experts on media interviews, written content, and other thought leadership storytelling.
  • Develop and optimize thought leadership content related to hosted and industry events, aligning event content to specific marketing campaigns when relevant.
  • Overseeing the creation of content by agency partners, interns, freelance copywriters; also writing and editing content.

You must be able to work independently in a structure with a North America-based manager, EMEA-based marketing squad, multitask, and adhere to strict deadlines. This role will involve occasional international and overseas travel.


Qualifications


Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • A degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field.
  • Proven relevant public relations and marketing experience (min 9 years) within a corporate or agency environment with demonstrable experience in PR planning, implementation, and evaluation.
  • Experience translating technical and industry-specific topics for Tier 1 media audiences.
  • Proven track record building relationships among Tier 1 journalists.
  • Experience collaborating with a global, distributed team required.
  • Fluent in modern communication and storytelling channels, i.e., social media, digital media.
  • B2B insurance sector or financial services experience desirable.
  • Thorough knowledge of the complete suite of Microsoft products and the ability to quickly learn new technologies.
  • Strong command of common AI workplace tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, etc.

Position Requirements:

  • Excellent communication skills and executive presence. Fluent English a pre-requisite, fluency in German or French would be a plus.
  • Have demonstrable skills in managing agencies, outside third parties and vendors to achieve overall communications objectives.
  • Adaptable work style and comfortable undertaking all levels of work assigned.
  • Must have strong organizational and project management skills, the ability to network within the organization, lead/influence project teams, and build consensus.
  • Must be comfortable working with senior management on a regular basis and the responsibilities and accountabilities that this brings.
  • Flexibility to travel.

In return, you will receive a competitive salary and benefits package which includes:

  • Private medical insurance contribution
  • Incentive Plan
  • Fitness Reimbursement Plan
  • 2 Global Well-being days per annum

FM is a people-driven business. It is our ability to harness the power of our diversity that allows us to create the unique, world-class services we’re known for. We’re committed to attracting a talented and diverse workforce and fostering a culture of inclusion that allows diversity to thrive and seed innovation.

title: Plant Superintendent
description:
As a Superintendent, you will lead the Converting Department to ensure safe, high-quality, and efficient production. You’ll oversee daily operations, lead and develop the department team, and work closely with other departments to meet production goals, maintain plant standards, and support continuous improvement.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead Supervisors and hourly employees across all shifts, ensuring consistent safety, quality, production, and housekeeping standards.
  • Maintain a strong presence on the production floor, providing real-time operational oversight and support to the Converting team.
  • Coordinate the performance of all shifts to ensure production schedules and department goals are met safely and efficiently.
  • Communicate plant standards, production expectations, and priorities clearly to the Converting team.
  • Work closely with Scheduling, Maintenance, and other departments to coordinate production needs and address issues that affect department performance.
  • Monitor production performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and communicate significant mechanical, scheduling, personnel, or operational concerns to plant leadership.
  • Ensure appropriate staffing, training, and cross-training within the department.
  • Conduct performance evaluations, provide coaching, and support employee development and skill growth.
  • Work closely with Maintenance to coordinate repairs and preventive maintenance and minimize production downtime.
  • Monitor equipment performance and ensure issues affecting production receive prompt attention.
  • Support and implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on production efficiency, quality, waste reduction, and equipment reliability.
  • Participate in the Safety Committee and promote a strong safety culture throughout the department.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies, safety programs, and housekeeping standards.
  • Build positive working relationships across departments and address employee concerns and conflicts appropriately.
  • Represent the Converting department professionally when interacting with customers or other external partners as needed.
  • Maintain required documentation and reporting.
  • Serve as a visible example of professionalism, accountability, punctuality, and consistent leadership.
  • Support continuous improvement efforts and assist with additional responsibilities as business needs require.

What You’ll Bring:

  • High school diploma or GED required; additional education or technical training preferred.
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience leading production teams across multiple shifts preferred.
  • Corrugated or converting experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, safety, quality, and production processes.
  • Strong communication, coaching, and employee relations skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, solve problems, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships across departments and hold teams accountable to established expectations.

What to Expect on the Job:

This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You’ll spend significant time on the production floor working directly with Supervisors and employees, monitoring operations, addressing issues, and supporting production goals, with time in the office for planning, communication, documentation, and administrative responsibilities.

You’ll work around moving mechanical equipment where noise, dust, vibration, and other typical manufacturing conditions are present. Our facility is not climate-controlled, so temperatures may vary throughout the year. Required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hearing protection, safety glasses, and protective footwear, must be worn in designated areas. Schedule flexibility may be required to support production needs, including occasional weekends.

What We Offer:

In addition to meaningful work and a sustainable mission, we offer competitive compensation plans, a full benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, All State, Pre-Paid Legal, and 401(k) with a company match. Benefits are effective the first day of the month following your hire date. You will also enjoy paid vacation, paid holidays and childbearing and parental leave.

description:
Join Our Team at Pratt Industries – Wapakoneta Corrugator!

At Pratt Industries, we’re committed to investing in your growth as much as you invest in us. If you’re looking for a company that values your skills and provides opportunities for career advancement, Pratt Industries is the perfect place for you! We recognize the value of your maintenance experience and reward it with competitive pay, excellent benefits, and unmatched career growth potential.

Why Work with Pratt Industries?

  • Great Career Opportunities: We are committed to developing our team members and providing opportunities for career growth at Pratt.
  • Fantastic Benefits:
    • Health Insurance & Wellness Program within 1 month of hire
    • Paid Holidays from Day 1
    • 401(k) with match
    • Paid vacation days
    • Tuition reimbursement & paid childbearing/parenting leave
    • $500 healthy lifestyles reimbursement program
    • Safety shoe and vision reimbursement program
    • And much more!


SUMMARY
Responsible for all activities associated with running the double-backer including setup, operation, cleanup, and recommending improvements to operations.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Set up bridge guides and glue station in accordance with proper setup techniques.
  • Check wet end lineups to verify correct roll stock is received and used.
  • Put rolls of paper in mill roll stands ensuring proper size and grade of paper to be run and make splices and paper changes as necessary.
  • Make adjustments during runs for tension, alignment, adhesion, and warp control.
  • Trim only the necessary amount of paper from the rolls when preparing for splices.
  • Remove roll stock from the machine when necessary and mark the proper size, grade, diameter, and lineal footage on the roll and place core plugs in each end of the buttrolls.
  • Maximize the utilization of equipment by operating the double-backer at available capacity and speed in line with those of the corrugator.
  • Clean starch pans, metering rolls, and glue rolls when necessary.
  • Keep the double backer area clean.
  • Complete necessary reports in an accurate and timely manner, including but not limited to: Production Data, Machine Operational Status, Safety Data, Quality Data.
  • Turn in maintenance work orders to supervisor for needed repairs. Be proactive in the maintenance of equipment.
  • Take all paper off of cores of stub rolls.
  • Assist the Corrugator Operator as necessary.
  • Assist in the training of dry end personnel.
  • Adheres to production schedule. Makes recommendations for optimizing the schedule to meet cost, quality and service goals.
  • Reports any unusual scheduling issues to Supervisor.
  • Comply with all company policies and procedures, including safety and maintaining good housekeeping.
  • Additional duties may be assigned by management.


EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
High school diploma or GED.


Candidates are PREFERRED who offer the following:
Prior work experience in the corrugated industry.
6 months’ experience on the dry end of the corrugator


LANGUAGE SKILLS
Able to read and follow instructions on factory masters.


MATHEMATICAL SKILLS
Able to read a tape measure with speed and accuracy. Able to calculate figures and amounts such as percentages, measurement, volume and rate. Able to apply concepts of high school math.


REASONING ABILITY
Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or graphic form. Ability to deal with problems involving one or more concrete variables in standardized situations.


TECHNICAL SKILLS
The individual must have a working knowledge of the following:
Equipment design and capabilities that can be translated into efficient operation.
Product layouts and production specifications
Product quality specifications
Quality standards


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS
May be required to maintain a current Lift Truck Operator License.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the functions of this job.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee is occasionally required to sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the functions of this job.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.


PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS
The performance of the employee will be measured as follows:
Operating standards - the employee will need to meet or exceed the Operating Standards in the areas of quality, cost, safety, customer satisfaction and productivity. Such standards will be set annually and communicated to the employee.
Personal growth - while the company will provide the tools to assist the employee to grow professionally the responsibility for moving forward lies with the individual. Each year there will be goals developed and agreed to by the employee and his/her superior.
Employee relations - through observations the employee will be evaluated regarding his/her behaviors associated with appropriate human interaction, respect and communication.
Creativity - this will be evaluated by how active the employee is in participating in advancing the business through new and innovative ideas.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Us

We are a world-class visitor attraction and leading science research centre. We use the Museum's unique collections and our unrivalled expertise to tackle the biggest challenges facing the world today. We care for more than 80 million objects spanning billions of years and welcome more than five million visitors annually and 16 million visits to our website.

Today the Museum is more relevant and influential than ever. By attracting people from a range of backgrounds to work for us, we can continue to look at the world with fresh eyes and find new ways of doing things.

We employ 1100 staff in a variety of roles, all united by our vision of a future where people and planet thrive. We need everyone to have the passion and drive to help us with our mission to create advocates for our planet and inspire millions to care about the natural world.

Diversity and inclusion matter to us.

Our vision is of a future where both people and the planet thrive. Diversity is one of our core values and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. All new staff who join us learn about the importance of diversity and inclusion to the Museum and how to contribute to creating an inclusive environment.

We know we have more to do, but we are committed to ensuring that everyone who works at the Museum feels they can thrive and feel valued and respected.

About the role

As a Software Engineer, you'll help build and support the backend services, integrations, and applications that underpin the Museum's digital experiences and business capabilities.

You’ll work with technologies including Java Spring Boot services and APIs, SQL and NoSQL databases, modern CI/CD pipelines, containerised deployments and cloud services, while collaborating closely with engineers, product managers and stakeholders across the Museum. You’ll play an active role in designing solutions, reviewing code, improving engineering practices, and helping ensure our systems remain secure, resilient, and maintainable.

This is an opportunity to work on meaningful products at scale, contribute across a broad technology landscape, and continue developing your skills within a supportive team that values learning, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

About you

We’re looking for a collaborative software engineer with experience developing backend applications in a production environment. You might already have strong experience with Java and Spring Boot, or you may have built similar backend services using related technologies and be keen to deepen your expertise.

You enjoy solving problems, learning new technologies, and working closely with others to deliver high-quality software. You’ll be familiar with modern engineering practices such as version control, code reviews, automated testing, and continuous integration, and you’ll appreciate the importance of security, reliability, and maintainability in everything you build.

We know that great candidates don’t always meet every listed requirement. If you’re excited about the role and can demonstrate strong software engineering fundamentals, we’d encourage you to apply.

Thriving at the Museum: the way we work

We are proud to work at the Museum and have identified the qualities we all need to embody to reach our shared ambition. This sits alongside the Museum’s values and forms the framework for the way we work.

Find out more here

What we offer

  • 27.5 days holiday plus 8 bank holidays (full time equivalent)
  • Generous defined contribution Natural History Museum Pension Scheme (employer contribution 4 - 10%)
  • Season ticket, bicycle and rental loan
  • Life insurance
  • Free admission to our exhibitions and many other paid exhibitions at museums, galleries and institutions across London and the UK.
  • Staff discount at our Museum shops and cafes
  • We offer a wide variety of training initiatives and opportunities to build skills. Investing in staff development is important to us, and we are ambitious about helping staff to grow and fulfil their potential.
  • Affordable membership to the Civil Service Sports Council which offers a range of benefits including an extensive list of special offers and reduced entry fees at a selection of cinema chains, theme parks, theatres, retailers and supermarkets. It also provides entry to up to 300 English Heritage sites and other national treasures. For more details, visit https://www.cssc.co.uk
  • Membership to our Sports and Social Association (for a small fee), which includes access to our in-house gym and clubs such as football, softball, table tennis and tennis and classes in Middle Eastern dance, yoga and Tai Chi

Hybrid working

We are working towards a vision where both people and planet thrive, and nothing gives a greater connection with this, than seeing first‑hand, the visitors, scientific research and collections that all of our work is inspired by and working side by side with the teams delivering the visitor experience and events. We also recognise the benefits and flexibility that hybrid working brings. We operate a hybrid working model that requires regular, weekly attendance for this role, with the precise pattern of days on site and worked from home to be agreed with your manager.

Closing date: 23:59 on 25 October 2026

Interviews expected: w/c 09 November 2026

Please note that this role does not qualify for Museum sponsorship so the successful postholder will need to have a valid right to work in the UK at the point of offer.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer, Video Intelligence
description:
NCS is a leading AI Tech Services company. With a 15,000-strong team across the Asia Pacific, NCS scales its platforms and capabilities to provide clients with greater agility and AI expertise across a range of Industries. Embracing a strong ecosystem of global partners, NCS transforms technology services delivery combining AI with digital resilience to drive real business impact. NCS is a subsidiary of the Singtel Group.

Job Description

We’re looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to own the security, reliability, and delivery of our Azure platform and Kubernetes workloads. You’ll be the hands‑on technical engineer for secure‑by‑default infrastructure—automating everything‑as‑code, and partnering with product teams to do deployment and enabling fast shipping of codes without trading off security or resilience.

Responsibilities

Platform engineering (Azure):

  • Build and evolve Azure Landing Zones, Management Group hierarchy, subscription vending, and policy-as-code guardrails using Azure Policy or equivalent tools.

Kubernetes (AKS)

  • Design & operate private AKS clusters (Azure CNI/Calico etc), implement Pod Security Standards, network policies (Calico/Cilium), workload identity (Entra OIDC/Workload Identity), and secure ingress/egress.

CI/CD & Supply Chain

  • Standardize pipelines in GitHub Actions / Azure DevOps; enforce SBOM, image scanning, cosign signing/verification, provenance (SLSA-aligned) and immutable deploys (GitOps with Argo CD/Flux).

Identity & Secrets

  • Implement Entra ID RBAC & PIM, Managed Identities, Key Vault / Secrets Store CSI, and secret rotation practices.

Observability & IR

  • Establish Azure Monitor / Log Analytics baselines, tracing, SLOs, and actionable alerts; integrate with Microsoft Sentinel; lead incident response and postmortems.

Cloud Security Posture

  • Drive Defender for Cloud coverage, vulnerability management (containers, hosts, code), and automated remediation.

Networking & Data Protection

  • Hub‑and‑spoke or vWAN, Private Link/Endpoints, Private DNS, Firewall/NAT Gateway egress control; encryption at rest & in transit, KMS integrations.

Resilience & DR

  • Backups (RSV/Velero), multi‑region patterns, chaos exercises, capacity planning; codify DR runbooks and perform tests.

FinOps & Compliance

  • Implement tagging/budgets, right‑sizing, Reservations/Savings Plans; map controls to CIS/NIST/ISO and produce audit evidence from pipelines.

Coaching & Enablement

  • Pair with product teams, review designs/PRs, write reference modules/templates, and uplift platform literacy across the org.

Security Hardening

  • Enable hardening for respective components, including but not limited to OS hardening, Application Hardening, Azure Services hardening.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years in DevOps/SRE/Platform Engineering with 3+ years on Azure and 2+ years operating Kubernetes in production.
  • Proven delivery of Azure Landing Zones or equivalent enterprise Azure foundations, expressed as Terraform or Bicep modules.
  • Strong with GitHub Actions/Azure DevOps, artifacts, environments, approvals, reusable workflows.
  • Hands‑on with container runtime security & policy: OPA/Gatekeeper or Kyverno, Pod Security restricted, read‑only root FS, capability drops, seccomp/AppArmor.
  • Network security in K8s: NetworkPolicy default‑deny, ingress controllers (Nginx/AGIC), egress control, TLS everywhere, mTLS preferred.
  • Image lifecycle: private registries (ACR), pull‑through caches, cosign signing & admission verification, Nessus scanning.
  • Observability: Azure Monitor/Logs, DCRs, dashboards, SLOs, alert routing to ITSM; experience integrating with Sentinel or enterprise SIEM.
  • Infra & config as code at scale; linting/testing/policy gates; change automation and drift detection (GitOps).
  • Solid Linux fundamentals, networking, PKI, and incident response.

Additional Information

We are driven by our AEIOU beliefs—Adventure, Excellence, Integrity, Ownership, and Unity—and we seek individuals who embody these values in both their professional and personal lives. We are committed to our Impact: Valuing our clients, Growing our people, and Creating our future.

Together, we make the extraordinary happen.

Learn more about us at ncs.co and visit our LinkedIn career site.

title: HGV Technician
description:
Adams Morey Plymouth is looking for a skilled and experienced HGV Technician to join our busy workshop team.

As an HGV Technician, you will be responsible for servicing, maintaining and repairing a range of commercial vehicles, ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently and to a high standard. You will play an important role in keeping our customers' vehicles on the road while delivering excellent workmanship and supporting the smooth running of the workshop.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced HGV Technician to join an established commercial vehicle dealership and develop their skills within a professional and supportive team.

Other duties may be required of the post holder in addition to those listed above and below, to ensure that the requirements of the business are met at all times.

Working hours: · Monday to Friday, Alternating Shifts, i.e. 40 hours per week, 30 minutes lunch break (unpaid), Week 1 – 7.00 am to 3.30 pm, Week 2 – 1.30 pm to 10.00 pm

Salary: OTE £50,000 per annum, dependent on experience, shift, qualifications and breakdown call outs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Carry out routine servicing, maintenance and repairs on a range of HGVs and commercial vehicles.

  • Diagnose mechanical, electrical and technical faults using appropriate diagnostic equipment.

  • Complete vehicle inspections and identify any defects or additional work required.

  • Carry out repairs in line with manufacturer specifications and company standards.

  • Ensure all work is completed safely, accurately and within agreed timescales.

  • Prepare vehicles for MOT testing and assist with any required remedial work.

  • Complete job cards, inspection sheets and other relevant paperwork accurately.

  • Identify and report any additional work required, ensuring it is communicated to the relevant team members.

  • Maintain a clean, tidy and safe working environment.

  • Ensure tools and workshop equipment are used correctly and maintained appropriately.

  • Keep up to date with relevant technical information, manufacturer guidance and changes within the industry.

  • Work closely with colleagues to ensure an efficient workflow within the workshop.

  • Follow all company policies, health and safety procedures and manufacturer requirements.

  • Carry out any other duties that may be required to meet the needs of the business.

Ideally, we are looking for:

  • Previous experience as an HGV Technician, Commercial Vehicle Technician or in a similar mechanical role.

  • Strong knowledge of HGV mechanical systems, maintenance and repair procedures.

  • Experience diagnosing and repairing mechanical and electrical faults.

  • A relevant Level 3 qualification in Heavy Vehicle Maintenance and Repair, or equivalent.

  • Good diagnostic and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent attention to detail and pride in the quality of your work.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

  • Good organisational skills and the ability to manage workload effectively.

  • A reliable, professional and safety-conscious approach.

  • A full UK driving licence would be advantageous, with relevant HGV driving licences also beneficial.

In return we’ll offer:

  • 30 days holidays including 8 bank holidays

  • Company sick pay, that increases with length of service up to 13 weeks

  • Company pension with the option to salary sacrifice

  • Where salary sacrifice takes place, 50% NI saving reinvested into your pension pot

  • Genuine career development and pathways with DAF Academy

  • Award winning apprenticeship program

  • Apprentice equipment scheme

  • Employee Assistance program

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • My Staff shop – access to hundreds of discounts

  • Quarterly More Awards recognition scheme

  • Free eye test vouchers for DSE users

  • On site parking (Site specific)

  • Free mortgage advice through a trusted partner

  • Qualified mental health first aiders

  • On-site trainer for HGV and many other courses

Who we are:

Adams Morey is a part of the Greenhous Group which holds a position as one of the leading independent commercial enterprises in the UK. With 21 sites across the UK, Greenhous are one of the largest group across the network.

Adams Morey itself was launched in 1973 and has successfully built an extensive customer base in the truck and van marketplace along the south coast. With its company headquarters in Southampton, we are the main DAF truck dealers in the area offering sales, parts and servicing.

AI Solution Integration & Delivery

  • AI‑enabled application development, including real‑time data‑driven applications, AI/ML and LLM integration, agentic workflows, and operational decision‑support systems

Quality Engineering & Secure Coding

  • Perform static code analysis, code reviews, and threat‑aware reviews of AI‑generated code and AI‑integrated features

DevOps & Continuous Delivery

  • Containerise applications and deploy to container platforms (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP)

Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing

  • Mentor junior developers on full stack engineering fundamentals and effective, responsible use of AI tools

Responsible AI & Engineering Excellence

  • Awareness of responsible AI principles, data privacy, IP considerations, and security implications of using AI tools on client engagements
  • Strong problem‑solving, analytical thinking, and sound judgement in when - and when not - to rely on AI‑generated output
  • Excellent written and spoken English, with strong communication and collaboration skills in a team environment
  • Self‑motivated, customer‑focused, and committed to high engineering and delivery standards

Additional Information

Why Join NCS

About Gallagher

Our purpose at Gallagher is 'Protect what matters most' and we live it every day, whetherthat'sprotecting the world's highest security environments or agricultural businesses, we care deeply about our people, their families, and our wider communities.

As we expand our Hamilton-based teams, this is your chance to be part of a true Kiwi tech success story making a global impact. Ifyou're driven by passion and purpose to protect what matters most, come help shape the future of what's possible with us.



About the Role

We're looking for Software Engineers at Junior, Intermediate and Senior level to join our High Security team in Hamilton.


This is one role open to all levels of experience, with the scope, technical ownership and support tailored to your level. Whether you're early in your software engineering career, an experienced developer looking for your next challenge, or a senior engineer ready to take on greater technical ownership, we'd love to hear from you.


You’ll contribute to the design, development and ongoing enhancement of our high-security products, used by customers around the world.


Working in a collaborative, cross-functional squad, you'll have the opportunity to work across front-end, back-end and embedded systems, solving complex technical problems and building robust, secure and high-quality software.



Security Clearance – Important Eligibility Requirement

To be considered for this role, you will be required to gain and maintain a security clearance to at least Confidential level.


To be eligible to obtain this security clearance, you must be an NZ permanent resident and have resided continuously in NZ or one of the Five Eyes countries (NZ, USA, UK, Canada or Australia) for the past 5 years.


Please check that you meet these requirements before applying.



About You

We're interested in hearing from Junior, Intermediate and Senior Software Engineers. You don't need to meet every requirement below. We're looking for strong engineering fundamentals, problem-solving ability, collaboration and a willingness to learn and grow.


C++ experience is essential. You may also bring experience in some of the following:

For Junior Engineers, we're interested in people with a solid foundation in software engineering who are keen to build their commercial experience and develop their skills in a product engineering environment.


For Intermediate and Senior Engineers, we're looking for stronger commercial experience and, depending on level, the ability to take increasing ownership of technical design, complex engineering problems and mentoring.



Working at Gallagher

You’ll be part of a global, future-focused organisation where creativity and innovation are valued and supported. Working in an environment driven by collaboration, innovation, passion, craftsmanship and mutual respect, you’ll help achieve our team purpose to translate vision into exceptional creations.


We also offer:

  • KiwiSaver on-top and Life and Disability insurance



  • Mentorship and professional development opportunities



  • A supportive team culture with team-building events, and a fun environment


Growth at Gallagher is constant, and we are building our team with like-minded individuals who relate to our story so that together we can continue to push the boundaries of what is possible.

title: Senior Product Builder
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Product Builder based in the United States.

As a Senior Product Builder, you will bridge product strategy and technical execution by rapidly designing, prototyping, and validating innovative payment solutions across mobile, desktop, and hardware platforms. You will transform merchant feedback and emerging market opportunities into functional proof-of-concept features, accelerating product development and reducing the time between ideas and implementation. Combining strong technical expertise with AI-powered development tools, you will build practical solutions that address real-world business needs. Working closely with merchants, sales partners, and engineering teams, you will define technical specifications and measurable evaluation criteria to ensure successful product delivery. You will also monitor industry trends and competitor innovations to identify opportunities for differentiation in the evolving payments landscape. This remote opportunity is ideal for a hands-on, technically minded product professional who thrives in fast-paced environments and values experimentation, user empathy, and tangible results.

Accountabilities

  • Define, design, and build end-to-end proof-of-concept features, interactive prototypes, and technical sandboxes for desktop applications, iOS and Android devices, payment terminals, and hardware kiosks.
  • Translate product concepts into detailed technical specifications, wireframes, schemas, and implementation-ready documentation, including employee permission rules, table mapping models, and product modifier customizations.
  • Establish clear product evaluation criteria and success metrics before feature development, enabling systematic testing, validation, and continuous improvement.
  • Conduct direct user discovery with merchants and sales partners to understand operational challenges, identify unmet needs, and rapidly translate feedback into functional solutions.
  • Accelerate product discovery and prototyping by leveraging large language model (LLM) APIs, prompt engineering, AI coding agents, and other modern development tools.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to ensure prototypes and technical specifications can be implemented efficiently, minimizing communication gaps and reducing development delays.
  • Monitor competitor product launches, point-of-sale innovations, and emerging payment technology trends to identify opportunities for new features and product enhancements.
  • Explore and validate capabilities such as drive-through modes, dark mode interfaces, item grids, group ordering, barcode scanning, and hardware customizations.
  • Build and test solutions across mobile, web, and payment hardware environments, ensuring that concepts are technically feasible and aligned with merchant requirements.
  • Work within Agile development environments to prioritize opportunities, manage product workflows, and accelerate delivery through iterative experimentation.
  • Maintain a strong focus on practical outcomes, continuously testing assumptions and delivering working prototypes rather than relying solely on presentations or theoretical product concepts.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree (BA or BS) or equivalent professional experience.
  • At least 8 years of experience in product management, product engineering, product analysis, or comparable technical product roles.
  • One to two years of experience working with AI tools, with practical knowledge of how to integrate them into product discovery, development, and prototyping workflows.
  • Strong technical fundamentals, including proficiency in SQL, JavaScript, and REST APIs or web APIs.
  • Hands-on experience developing native or cross-platform applications for iOS and Android.
  • Familiarity with payment hardware ecosystems, including card readers, point-of-sale terminals, and self-service kiosks.
  • Strong working knowledge of LLM APIs, prompt engineering, AI-assisted coding agents, and AI-driven development workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating with Agile software development teams and translating product requirements into actionable technical deliverables.
  • Proficiency with Jira and modern product management tools for planning, prioritization, documentation, and delivery tracking.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate technical feasibility, validate hypotheses, and make informed product decisions.
  • Strong user empathy and discovery skills, with the ability to engage merchants and sales partners, understand their needs, and translate insights into practical solutions.
  • A proactive, builder-first mindset, with a strong bias toward experimentation, rapid execution, and demonstrable results.
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, particularly when working across product, engineering, and commercial teams.
  • Product Owner certification, such as Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), is preferred.
  • Previous experience in payments, financial technology (fintech), or point-of-sale solutions is highly desirable.
  • Eligibility to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, as sponsorship is not available for this position.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: Annual salary range of $104,000–$149,000, depending on work location, relevant skills, qualifications, and experience.
  • Medical coverage: Comprehensive medical insurance.
  • Dental and vision: Dental and vision insurance coverage.
  • Flexible paid time off: Flexible PTO to support personal needs and work-life balance.
  • Retirement savings: 401(k) plan with employer matching contributions.
  • Mental health and well-being: Access to mental health support and a dedicated well-being program.
  • Paid parental leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave.
  • Education assistance: Support for continuing education and professional development.
  • Lifestyle spending account: Company-funded allowance for eligible lifestyle and personal well-being expenses.
  • Remote work: A remote working arrangement for eligible candidates based in the United States.
  • Inclusive work environment: An opportunity to collaborate with a diverse team of innovators and contribute to the development of modern payment technology.

title: Converting Supervisor
description:
POSITION TITLE: CONVERTING SUPERVISOR - 2ND SHIFT

REPORTS TO: Converting Superintendent

SUMMARY

Supervise approximately 2 – 30 people in the daily routine of producing quality corrugated products in a safe, productive manner with minimum waste. Cross-train employees in key positions.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintain quality, efficiencies, and production levels set by management. Communicate these standards to your staff.
  • Report quality concerns to Converting and Plant Superintendent. Assist in determining quality guidelines.
  • Establish high morale within your department by showing fairness, consistency, and an interest in employee problems. Maintain confidentiality.
  • Maintain inventories of sheets, inks and other converting supplies.
  • Coordinate with your supervisor and Maintenance Superintendent on any repairs or preventive maintenance done in the department.
  • Keep upper management informed of problems or situations that may affect the performance of your department.
  • Enforce the corrective action procedures when applicable and conduct meetings with the violating employees
  • Conduct weekly Production/Safety meetings with departmental personnel.
  • Communicate with necessary supervision to avoid problems between shift changes.
  • Improve career skills by enrolling yourself in seminars, technical courses, and related college courses.
  • Implement, maintain, and support all company policies and procedures.
  • Comply with company policies and procedures.
  • Additional duties may be assigned by management.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Directly supervises all employees assigned to the department.
  • Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws.
  • Responsibilities include training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; conflict resolution; team building; coaching and leading employees to improve; addressing complaints and resolving problems; documentation; and setting an example of superior behavior, attitude and performance.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Two years prior supervisory experience.

REQUIRED:

  • Prior work experience in the corrugated industry.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

  • Able to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
  • Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
  • Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or employees of organization.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

  • Able to read a tape measure with speed and accuracy.
  • Able to calculate figures and amounts such as percentages, measurement, volume and rate. Able to apply concepts of high school math.

REASONING ABILITY

  • Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or graphic form.
  • Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

The individual must have a working knowledge of the following:

  • Equipment design and capabilities that can be translated into efficient operation. This also supports the supervisor's role of teacher and trainer for his/her personnel.
  • Cost issues in order to make daily decisions that will reduce overall costs and will help the supervisor find areas that require improvement.
  • Quality standards.
  • Regulatory requirements including but not limited to wage and hour requirements, environmental and waste minimization, company policies, and personnel requirements including OSHA, DEQ and EEO.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • May be required to maintain a current Lift Truck Operator License.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the functions of this job.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and talk or hear.
  • The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
  • The employee is occasionally required to sit.
  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the functions of this job.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts.
  • The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions.
  • The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; and vibration.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

LEADERSHIP ATTRIBUTES

The individual must possess the following:

  • Superior time management skills including the ability to manage multiple issues concurrently and the ability to lead an effective and efficient meeting.
  • Teaching skills in order to function effectively as a teacher for his personnel both in the technical and administrative parts of the position.
  • Excellent crisis manager who demonstrates that he/she has a high emotional control under adverse conditions and can lead his/her personnel to a successful resolution.
  • Excellent employee relations skills including being an active listener, understanding how to appraise personnel, applying both positive and corrective feedback, being able to resolve conflicts either involving the supervisor directly or as a third party, understands and demonstrates positive motivational skills including coaching and delegation techniques.
  • Demonstrated confidence including providing a consistent leadership style with an acceptable level of professional assertiveness.

PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS

The performance of the supervisor will be measured as follows:

  • Operating standards - the supervisor will need to meet or exceed the Operating Standards in the areas of quality, cost, safety, customer satisfaction and productivity. Such standards will be set annually and communicated to the supervisor.
  • Personal growth - while the company will provide the tools to assist the supervisor to grow professionally the responsibility for moving forward lies with the individual. Each year there will be goals developed and agreed to by the supervisor and his/her superior.
  • Employee relations - through observations the supervisor will be evaluated regarding his/her skills and advancements in the areas of motivational techniques and results, positive and corrective/constructive feedback, subordinate development and creating a positive work environment.
  • Creativity - this will be evaluated by how active the supervisor is in participating in advancing the business through new and innovative ideas.

title: Electrical and Instrumentation Lead Technician
description:
Position Summary

The Electrical & Instrumentation Lead Technician is responsible for leading electrical and instrumentation maintenance activities throughout the paper manufacturing facility. This position ensures the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of electrical systems, process controls, instrumentation, and automation equipment. The Lead Technician provides technical guidance to maintenance team members, troubleshoots equipment issues, and supports continuous improvement efforts to maximize production uptime.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate electrical and instrumentation maintenance activities during assigned shifts.
  • Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain electrical systems, motor controls, PLCs, drives, instrumentation, and process control equipment.
  • Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance on production equipment.
  • Support paper machine, converting equipment, utilities, and plant infrastructure.
  • Assist with equipment installations, upgrades, and capital improvement projects.
  • Ensure compliance with all safety policies, lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and electrical safety standards.
  • Read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, and technical manuals.
  • Train and mentor maintenance technicians on electrical and instrumentation systems.
  • Work closely with operations personnel to minimize downtime and improve equipment reliability.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation in the maintenance management system.
  • Participate in troubleshooting during emergencies and production outages.
  • Support continuous improvement and reliability initiatives throughout the facility.
  • On Call

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required; technical degree or apprenticeship preferred.
  • Minimum 5 years of industrial electrical and instrumentation maintenance experience.
  • Experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably paper, pulp, converting, or other heavy industrial operations.
  • Working knowledge of:
    • PLC systems (Allen-Bradley preferred)
    • Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)
    • Motors and motor controls
    • Instrumentation and process controls
    • Electrical troubleshooting and diagnostics
  • Ability to read electrical schematics and technical diagrams.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Previous project planning and managing.

Physical Requirements

  • Frequently stand, walk, climb ladders, bend, and lift-up to 50 pounds.
  • Work in industrial manufacturing conditions including heat, noise, dust, and varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to work rotating shifts, weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed.

Key Competencies

  • Leadership
  • Troubleshooting and Diagnostics
  • Electrical Safety Compliance
  • Preventive Maintenance
  • Reliability Improvement
  • Teamwork and Communication
  • Continuous Improvement

This position plays a key role in maintaining safe and reliable plant operations while supporting production goals and minimizing equipment downtime.

title: Principal Robotics Hardware Engineer
description:
In this role, you will take on challenges in TELEXISTENCE's robot development where the technical approach or feasibility is not yet clear, and drive them to resolution yourself. Grounded in robot hardware development, you will solve problems across all disciplines, not only from the mechanical, electrical, and software perspectives.

As a Principal, you are expected to own the full path to solving the problems that block development: defining what needs to be solved, building hypotheses from first principles, exploring approaches, prototyping and experimenting, and feeding the results into the design. Even when no established solution exists, you will find a path to realization through validation, and you will be responsible for delivering hardware that actually works and can be used on an ongoing basis.

You will also support engineers in each specialized area on the technical side, and lead both the resolution of critical issues that go beyond individual teams and the technical decision-making for the robot system as a whole. You will also do hands-on design, assembly, and experiments yourself.

Key Responsibilities

Solving technical problems with no clear path forward

  • For problems where the requirements, root causes, or solutions are unclear, define the target state and constraints, and separate known facts from unverified hypotheses.

  • Return to the underlying principles of mechanics, mechanisms, materials, manufacturing, and related fields to develop multiple candidate solutions. Plan experiments to validate the most critical and uncertain issues, and manage your own work as well as internal and external resources to carry out prototyping, measurement, and evaluation.

  • When an extension of the existing configuration will not work, explore alternatives with stakeholders, including revisiting the requirements, and lead changes to mechanisms, configurations, components, and manufacturing methods.

  • Own the entire process, from identifying problems and proposing direction to implementation, confirming effectiveness on the actual hardware, and preventing the root problem from recurring, so that the team can move on to the next stage of development.

System design and development for sustained operation

  • For existing robots, devices for collecting learning data, and other systems, decide the mechanical system architecture, key interfaces, and performance allocation. Work with electrical, controls, and software specialists to resolve design issues.

  • Reflect constraints from component sourcing, manufacturing, and assembly in design decisions, and own the technical side from prototyping through building the required number of units, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

  • Identify the root causes of failures that occur in testing and operation, validate required performance, reliability, and maintainability, and confirm that countermeasures are effective.

Technical leadership across teams

  • Provide technical support, design reviews, and mentoring to development team members, including Lead and Expert engineers, and personally take ownership of the hardest problems to chart a path to their resolution.

  • Communicate technical risks and validation results clearly, and bring stakeholders to agreement on development priorities, required resources, and whether to continue or change course.

  • Share the design rationale, failure cases, and evaluation methods gained through problem-solving in a form other members can reuse, raising the organization's problem-solving capability.

Requirements: Must-Haves

Technical skills

  • 7+ years of hands-on experience making design decisions by combining deep knowledge of mechanisms, drive systems, materials, strength and stiffness, and tolerancing with quantitative analysis and validation on physical hardware.

  • Ability to design with 3D CAD, create drawings, design for manufacturing and assembly, and personally carry out assembly, evaluation, and failure analysis.

  • Understanding of constraints related to sensors, actuators, electrical components, wiring, and thermal management, and the ability to discuss system-level issues with electrical, controls, and software engineers.

Professional experience

  • Extensive hands-on experience developing robots, mechatronic systems, or complex mechanical equipment, including taking ownership from concept through evaluation on physical hardware.

  • A track record of solving technical problems with no precedent or established approach by forming your own hypotheses and validating them through prototyping and experiments. You should be able to explain your technical decisions, their rationale, and the results in concrete terms.

  • Experience leading technical problems that span multiple disciplines and contributing to other engineers' results through design reviews and technical guidance.

Other

  • Ability to turn unknowns and failures into concrete validation tasks and to persist until they are solved.

  • Ability to step into whatever areas are needed while anchored in your own expertise, incorporate insights from other specialists, and update hypotheses and designs based on experimental results.

  • Willingness to take responsibility for the whole robot actually working, both through your own technical output and through supporting others.

  • Ability to hold technical discussions and negotiations with domestic and international suppliers, and to drive internal technical discussions and collaboration in English.

Requirements: Nice-to-Haves

End effectors and Leader/Follower systems

  • Component-level design and development experience with end effectors, actuators, or robot arms.

  • Experience designing and implementing Leader devices, including developing and evaluating mechanisms that capture the operator's hand and arm motion, operation-assist mechanisms, and operator interfaces.

  • Experience designing and implementing robot hands on the Follower side, including evaluating mechanism, drive, and sensor configurations, and evaluating and improving grasping and manipulation performance, durability, and cost.

  • Experience integrating and implementing Leader–Follower teleoperation systems, including implementing and evaluating motion mapping between the two devices, position and force measurement, calibration, and haptics.

  • Experience developing physical hardware and data collection systems for imitation learning or reinforcement learning, or collaborating with learning/ML teams.

  • Experience with force and tactile sensors, compliant mechanisms, and compact power transmission mechanisms.

Actuator development

  • Experience breaking down a robot's actuator requirements, calculating theoretical values against those requirements, and selecting components such as reducers, motors, encoders, and bearings that meet them.

  • Experience customizing the components themselves for overall optimization, not just combining off-the-shelf parts, or experience developing and evaluating components such as reducers and motors yourself.

  • Experience evaluating and improving actuator durability and cost, and negotiating with partners on manufacturing and procurement.

Mass production

  • Experience turning research-stage technology into equipment or products that can be used on an ongoing basis, and solving unit-to-unit variation, calibration, and maintenance issues when deploying multiple units.

  • Experience taking a product from prototype to a production ramp-up of roughly 100–1,000 units.

Other

  • Ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced, highly goal-oriented environment.

  • Ability to find optimal yet practical mechanical design solutions under tight deadlines.

  • Experience designing with 3D CAD (experience with SolidWorks is a plus).

  • Practical experience with risk assessment and an understanding of relevant laws and regulations.

  • Dicing
  • Optical inspection
  • Wirebonding of chips inside sample holders

The team is in charge of:

  • operating the tools for the regular delivery of test chips
  • developing/improving new processes (for better quality/leadtime/chip selection…)
  • overseeing its own tools (daily check of the tools, ensuring maintenance schedules are followed, 1 level of troubleshooting)
  • selection, installation and qualification of new tools

Responsabilities

About the Role

As a Test & Characterization Engineer within the Nanofabrication Backend Team, you will play a critical role in validating our fabrication processes, ensuring data reliability, and developing innovative testing methodologies for superconducting qubits. You will contribute to improving wafer and chip performance through rigorous device testing, robust metrology, and collaborative problem-solving across teams.
  • Develop and optimize superconducting qubit testing methods at room and cryogenic temperatures, providing fast feedback to nanofabrication processes and ensuring efficient sorting of chips.
  • Collaborate with design and process integration teams to define and evaluate test structures that improve wafer- and chip-level performance.
  • Ensure accuracy and reliability of equipment metrology, data acquisition systems and inspection equipment.
  • Contribute to the identification, procurement, and validation of new test and metrology equipment for the backend nanofabrication line.
  • Implement continuous improvement plans to enhance testing efficiency, reliability, and throughput.
  • Perform device testing at room and cryogenic temperatures, ensuring accurate and reproducible results.
  • Participate in failure analysis and root cause investigations, helping to close the loop between design, fabrication, and performance.

Requirements

  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with device testing, electrical measurements, or semiconductor/metrology equipment.
  • Familiarity with superconducting devices or cryogenic measurements is a strong plus.
  • Proficiency with data acquisition systems, lab instrumentation, and analysis tools (e.g., LabVIEW, Python, MATLAB, JMP).
  • Strong problem-solving mindset, analytical rigor, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment.
  • Languages: Proficient in English; French is a plus
